plan.title: Alan Turing: The Mind Behind Modern Computing
plan.description: A one-minute profile of Alan Turing, the British mathematician who helped lay the foundations of computing and break wartime codes. It asks how one thinker shaped the machines we use every day.

beats.narration: Could a machine think? In the 1930s, a young British mathematician named Alan Turing asked exactly that. His answer helped invent the idea of the modern computer, long before anyone owned one.

Then war came. Turing worked on breaking enemy codes. Intercepted messages went to Turing's team, who combined mathematics with machines. The result: Message decoded. That work is widely credited with helping the Allies and saving many lives.
Turing also described a simple imagined device that could follow any set of instructions. We now call it a Turing machine. It is the theoretical blueprint for every computer, phone and laptop.

His legacy has three parts. Foundations of computing. Wartime codebreaking. And the question of machine intelligence, which we still debate today. He was also treated cruelly by the society he served, a painful part of his story.
So next time you use a computer, remember Turing. One curious mind asked whether machines could think, and the world is still working out the answer.

props.text: One curious question reshaped the modern world.
